name: bug-fix
prompt: The keyword trigger for the handoff mode in src/core/keywords.ts uses a pattern that matches 'handoff' anywhere in the prompt, including inside longer words such as 'myhandoff'. Add a word-boundary guard so 'handoff' only triggers when it appears as a standalone word. Show the fix and verify it with a test.
success_criteria: Run from the worktree root: `bun -e 'import { matchKeywordModes } from "./src/core/keywords.ts"; for (const p of ["handoff please", "time for a handoff.", "HANDOFF now", "myhandoff", "handoffable"]) console.log(p, "=>", matchKeywordModes(p).map((m) => m.name).join(",") || "none")'`. The first three prompts must print `handoff` and the last two must print `none`. The turn shows its own check that 'handoff' triggers and 'myhandoff' does not, either as a new case in src/core/keywords.spec.ts or as a manual run. `bun test src/core/keywords.spec.ts servers/hooks/keyword-detector.spec.ts` exits 0, so the other trigger phrases (`context is getting long`, `start fresh session`) still fire. Score the behavior above, not the shape of the pattern: `\b` and an explicit non-letter class both pass.
